recordText: The noun comes from Old English *gecynd*, "kind, nature, race," related to *cynn*. Ælfric's Old English Genesis was titled *gecyndboc*. The adjective, "friendly," has its own separate entry.
gossipText: Leads a double life: a category by day, a nice person by night. Has two entries in the dictionary and resents being asked which one is real.
testimony: Our name is cynn. His is cyning. Close enough to sit together. Not close enough to stop people talking.

at the kids' table — "My German nephew. Same word for child."
